scr_ap_creating_an_a_p_invoice_for_a_tra.purpose: Turns an approved purchase order or subcontract sitting in the spend management workbench into an actual A/P invoice — carrying the matched order's vendor, property and coding forward while the accountant still supplies invoice date, invoice number, due date and the accounting period that decides which month the expense lands in.
scr_ap_creating_an_a_p_invoice_for_a_tra.outcome: A posted liability that credits 2010 Accounts Payable in the period the work was received and debits the same expense line the PO committed, with the order's remaining balance drawn down by the invoiced amount.
scr_ap_creating_an_a_p_invoice_for_a_tra.rootCause: The workbench hands you a pre-coded invoice, and that convenience is exactly the trap: the defaults come from the order, not from the invoice in front of you. A December roof patch invoiced in January still belongs in December, and a PO coded to 6110 Repairs & Maintenance may be carrying work that betters the roof and belongs in 1530 Building Improvements. Nobody re-examines coding a machine supplied.
scr_ap_creating_an_a_p_invoice_for_a_tra.ifSkipped: Committed spend never converts to a payable, so the property shows an understated 2010 balance and the expense drops into whatever month someone eventually keys it.
gaap: ASC 405-10 — recognition of the liability when the obligation arises
Treas. Reg. §1.263(a)-3 — betterment/restoration versus routine repair
COSO 2013 — Principle 10, three-way match before the payable posts
redFlags: Invoice date and accounting period pointing at different months with no accrual explanation
Invoice amount exceeding the PO balance with no change order behind it
Every workbench-created invoice landing on the PO's default expense account, even the capital ones
scr_ap_creating_an_a_p_invoice_for_a_tra.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Purchase Order > 'Create Payable' from the approved PO, or PAYscan invoice register matched to the PO.

scr_ap_paying_an_a_p_invoice_for_a_trans.purpose: Opens a posted or partially paid A/P invoice straight from the spend management workbench and runs the payment against it, so the same session that reviewed the transaction can release the disbursement without returning to the payments module.
scr_ap_paying_an_a_p_invoice_for_a_trans.outcome: Payment posts DR 2010 Accounts Payable / CR 1110 Operating Cash against the property's authorized bank account, and the invoice drops off the vendor's open aging.
scr_ap_paying_an_a_p_invoice_for_a_trans.rootCause: This is the screen where approval and disbursement collapse into one pair of hands. A regional manager who approved the subcontract can, one click later, pay it — no second reviewer, no check-run batch, no positive-pay gate. Where the approval policy's dollar limits do not also constrain payment rights, the segregation of duties that the whole workflow was built to enforce evaporates at the last step.
scr_ap_paying_an_a_p_invoice_for_a_trans.ifSkipped: Approved invoices wait for the next scheduled check run, which is the correct outcome for most spend but causes a real late fee on a utility or tax payment with a hard due date.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 10, segregation of approval from disbursement
NACHA Operating Rules — authorization and formatting for ACH debits
31 CFR Part 501 — OFAC screening of the payee before funds move
redFlags: The same user id appearing as both final approver and payer on the transaction's history
Workbench payments made outside the weekly run with no exception documentation
Payments released without checking the property's available operating cash
scr_ap_paying_an_a_p_invoice_for_a_trans.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Check Processing or the 'Pay' action on an individual payable; ACH via Payables > EFT file generation.

scr_ap_closing_a_transaction.purpose: Marks a purchase order or subcontract complete from the workbench so no further invoices can be billed against it, releasing the unspent commitment back to the property's available budget.
scr_ap_closing_a_transaction.outcome: The order shows closed (or 'Full invoice match' where auto-close is disabled for subcontracts) and its residual commitment stops consuming budget capacity.
scr_ap_closing_a_transaction.rootCause: Commitments that stay open after the work is finished distort two things at once: the budget looks more consumed than it is, so site teams are told they have no money left for a turn, and month-end accrual reviewers cannot tell a genuinely received-not-invoiced obligation from a stale PO nobody closed. On subcontracts with retainage, closing early is worse — it strands the 2015 Retainage Payable balance with no open contract to bill it against.
scr_ap_closing_a_transaction.ifSkipped: Stale open orders inflate committed cost, understate available budget, and force the accountant to age every open PO by hand at close to work out which ones still need an accrual.
gaap: ASC 440-10 — commitments and their disclosure
COSO 2013 — Principle 12, controls over commitment records
State mechanic's lien statutes — final lien waiver before a construction contract is closed
redFlags: Subcontracts closed while retainage is still payable
Orders closed to clear a budget check rather than because work finished
Auto-close disabled on subcontracts with nobody assigned to close them manually
scr_ap_closing_a_transaction.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Purchase Order > 'Close PO' flag, and Job Cost contract close-out with final retainage release.

scr_ap_canceling_a_transaction.purpose: Voids an unfulfilled purchase order, subcontract or service order from the workbench — including cancelling one service order inside a service contract via its Detail link — so a commitment made in error never becomes a payable.
scr_ap_canceling_a_transaction.outcome: The transaction moves to cancelled status with the audit trail intact and its committed amount removed from budget consumption.
scr_ap_canceling_a_transaction.rootCause: A cancelled order and a closed order look similar on a budget report and mean opposite things to a reviewer: closed means the money was spent, cancelled means it never will be. Teams reach for Cancel when a vendor partially performed, which is wrong — partial performance needs the received portion invoiced and the remainder closed, or the property escapes a liability it genuinely owes.
scr_ap_canceling_a_transaction.ifSkipped: Dead commitments keep eating budget capacity and show up in the committed-cost column of every owner report until someone manually reconciles the PO register.
gaap: ASC 440-10 — derecognition of a commitment that will not be performed
IRC §6001 — the cancelled record and its reason are retained, never deleted
COSO 2013 — Principle 13, quality information about open obligations
redFlags: Cancellations on orders where the vendor already delivered part of the scope
No cancellation reason recorded, leaving the audit trail silent about why
Repeated cancel-and-reissue on the same vendor and scope, a classic way to stay under an approval threshold
scr_ap_canceling_a_transaction.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Purchase Order > 'Cancel PO', or Service Contract > cancel the individual work order line.

scr_ap_adding_approval_policies_2.purpose: Builds an approval policy in the Approval Policy Manager — choosing the policy type (amount, tiered amount, vendor, job type) and mapping each tier to the role or user who must sign off, which is where the owner's delegation-of-authority matrix stops being a PDF and becomes enforced system behavior.
scr_ap_adding_approval_policies_2.outcome: Transactions at or above each defined threshold route to the named approver, and the routing is evidenced in every transaction's approval history.
scr_ap_adding_approval_policies_2.rootCause: Management agreements delegate spending authority in dollar bands — a site manager to $2,500, a regional to $10,000, the asset manager above that — and auditors test whether the system actually enforces those bands. A policy built with a gap between tiers, or a top tier with no ceiling, lets an invoice route to the wrong level and no exception report will ever flag it.
scr_ap_adding_approval_policies_2.ifSkipped: Spend routes by default or not at all, and the delegation-of-authority matrix in the management agreement becomes unenforceable and untestable.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 10, authorization limits embedded in control activities
Management agreement delegation-of-authority provisions
SOC 1 — control design over transaction authorization
reports: Exception report of transactions posted without approval
redFlags: Gaps or overlaps between the Amount from and Amount to bands
A top tier with no upper bound and only one approver
Policies naming a specific user rather than a role, which fails silently when that person leaves
scr_ap_adding_approval_policies_2.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Administration > Workflow setup, approval tiers by amount and property with role-based approvers.

scr_ap_changing_an_approver_of_a_transac.purpose: Edits an existing approval policy to swap the role or user in a routing tier, used when a regional manager changes properties, an approver leaves, or a level needs a backup during a long absence.
scr_ap_changing_an_approver_of_a_transac.outcome: Transactions newly entering that tier route to the replacement approver, while the history of items already approved keeps naming the original approver.
scr_ap_changing_an_approver_of_a_transac.rootCause: Approver changes are made under pressure — invoices are stuck, the vendor is calling — and the person making the swap often does not check whether the replacement's own permissions cover the property or the dollar band. A user who lacks rights to the property simply never sees the item, so the invoice moves from one silent queue to another and the A/P aging keeps growing with nobody accountable.
scr_ap_changing_an_approver_of_a_transac.ifSkipped: Transactions stall in a queue belonging to someone who has left or cannot see the property, and invoices age past terms with no approver to escalate to.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 3, assignment of authority and responsibility
SOX 404 — evidence that approvers held valid authority on the date of approval
Management agreement delegation-of-authority provisions
redFlags: Approver changed to someone without property-level permissions, so items disappear from all queues
Temporary delegations left in place months after the absence ended
The requester of the change and the new approver being the same person
scr_ap_changing_an_approver_of_a_transac.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Administration > Workflow setup > edit the approval step's assigned role or user.

scr_ap_auto_approving_transaction_amount.purpose: Documents the built-in behavior of amount and tiered-amount policies whereby RealPage skips every approval tier at or below the submitter's own authority — so a CFO entering an invoice does not wait for the property manager and regional manager to approve beneath them.
scr_ap_auto_approving_transaction_amount.outcome: Transactions entered by senior staff clear the lower tiers instantly and route only to approvers above the submitter's level, or post immediately if the submitter outranks all tiers.
scr_ap_auto_approving_transaction_amount.rootCause: This is self-approval by design, and it is the single behavior in the approval engine most likely to surprise an auditor. A senior user who enters an invoice within their own band posts it with no second pair of eyes at all — creation and approval in one person. It is defensible only if the controls compensating for it (post-hoc review of senior-entered transactions, a vendor-master control, a bank rec by someone else) are real and documented.
scr_ap_auto_approving_transaction_amount.ifSkipped: Staff misread the workbench as having approved items that the engine simply bypassed, and the compensating review over senior-entered spend never gets designed.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 10, segregation of duties and compensating controls
AU-C 240 / PCAOB AS 2401 — management override of controls
SOX 404 — design effectiveness of the authorization control
reports: Journal entry and invoice audit trail
redFlags: Senior users routinely entering their own invoices rather than submitting through site staff
No monitoring report over transactions that cleared via submitter-level auto-approval
Approval limits raised for a user shortly before a large transaction is entered by that same user
scr_ap_auto_approving_transaction_amount.yardi: Yardi Voyager: workflow steps configured to skip when the originator's authority already covers the amount; reviewed via the workflow audit log.

scr_ap_submitter_conditions_in_approval_.purpose: Sets a workflow to fire only when a named user or user role submits the transaction — or on everyone except that user or role — by setting the condition's policy type to Submitter or Submitter role.
scr_ap_submitter_conditions_in_approval_.outcome: The workflow applies selectively by who entered the item, so one entity can run a tighter path for site-entered spend and a lighter one for corporate-entered spend.
scr_ap_submitter_conditions_in_approval_.rootCause: Submitter conditions are how a portfolio handles the accountant who enters invoices on behalf of ten properties: without them, every item that offshore team keys routes as if the site manager had entered it. The exclusion form is the dangerous one — 'apply to everyone except Kim Johnson' means Kim's transactions route through no workflow at all, and reading the condition list months later nobody remembers why.
scr_ap_submitter_conditions_in_approval_.ifSkipped: One workflow governs all submitters, so either corporate entries crawl through site-level approvals or site entries slip through corporate-level ones.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 10, tailoring control activities to the risk of the originator
SOX 404 — completeness of the authorization control population
SOC 1 — control design documented for user entities
reports: Transactions posted without a workflow match
redFlags: Exclusion conditions naming an individual with no documented business reason
Submitter conditions that leave a class of transactions matching no workflow at all
Conditions written against a user id that has since been reassigned to a different person
scr_ap_submitter_conditions_in_approval_.yardi: Yardi Voyager: workflow conditions keyed to the originating user or user group in Administration > Workflow setup.

scr_ap_approval_workbench_4.purpose: The central queue where every transaction type awaiting approval — A/P invoices, purchase orders, subcontracts, journal entries, expense reports — is filtered, reviewed, approved, declined, closed, reassigned to another approver or exported to Excel.
scr_ap_approval_workbench_4.outcome: An approver sees one prioritized list of everything blocking the close or the check run and can dispose of each item without navigating to its home module.
scr_ap_approval_workbench_4.rootCause: The workbench is where the A/P aging is really controlled. An invoice that never leaves this queue never posts, so the 2010 Accounts Payable balance on the owner's balance sheet is short by whatever is sitting here on the last day of the month. Most portfolios discover this only when an accrual review asks why the aging does not agree to the invoices physically on hand.
scr_ap_approval_workbench_4.ifSkipped: Approvals happen ad hoc through email and module-by-module screens, items are missed, and month-end accruals miss everything still pending.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 10, centralized evidence of authorization
ASC 405-10 — completeness of recorded liabilities at the reporting date
SOX 404 — operating effectiveness of the approval control
redFlags: Items pending approval for more than a week at month-end with no accrual booked
A queue that is empty only because the filter excludes a transaction type
Approvers using the workbench export as their review record rather than opening the invoice image
scr_ap_approval_workbench_4.yardi: Yardi Voyager: the 'My Approvals' inbox plus PAYscan invoice register workflow queues.

scr_ap_viewing_the_approval_workbench_3.purpose: Covers reading the workbench as a requester or approver — choosing between the View all and My approvals perspectives, selecting the transaction type, and applying the remaining filters before clicking Apply.
scr_ap_viewing_the_approval_workbench_3.outcome: The list shown matches the intended scope, so an approver works their own queue and a requester can see where their submissions are stuck.
scr_ap_viewing_the_approval_workbench_3.rootCause: View all and My approvals answer different questions and are constantly confused. An approver who leaves the page on View all clears items assigned to colleagues; a controller checking coverage on My approvals sees an empty queue and concludes nothing is outstanding when forty invoices are sitting with a regional manager on leave. The filter state persists, so the mistake repeats every session.
scr_ap_viewing_the_approval_workbench_3.ifSkipped: Approvers work from an unfiltered or wrongly scoped list, miss their own items and approve other people's, and requesters chase status by phone.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 10, approval by the individual with delegated authority
SOX 404 — evidence that the correct approver acted
SOC 1 — user access scoped to the approver's own responsibilities
redFlags: Approvers habitually working in View all rather than My approvals
A transaction-type filter left set from a previous session hiding an entire category
Pending items visible to nobody because every eligible approver's queue filters them out
scr_ap_viewing_the_approval_workbench_3.yardi: Yardi Voyager: 'My Approvals' versus the full workflow queue filtered by property and transaction type.

scr_ap_viewing_and_editing_transactions_.purpose: The View and Edit actions on a workbench row, which let an approver open the transaction, change it before deciding — including expense-report lines where selecting Gasoline with a tax rate opens a mileage box and recalculates the amount on save — and then approve or decline.
scr_ap_viewing_and_editing_transactions_.outcome: Corrections are made in-line by the approver, saved to the transaction, and the item continues through the workflow already fixed.
scr_ap_viewing_and_editing_transactions_.rootCause: Edit-then-approve compresses preparer and reviewer into one action. The approver who fixes the GL code and immediately approves has reviewed their own correction, and the approval history will show them approving a transaction they materially changed. On expense reports the recalculation makes it worse: the amount an approver signs off on is not the amount they read a moment earlier.
scr_ap_viewing_and_editing_transactions_.ifSkipped: Every coding error bounces back to the submitter for rekeying, which adds days to the cycle and pushes invoices past the accrual cut-off.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 10, preparer and reviewer must be distinct
IRS Publication 463 / accountable plan rules — mileage substantiation
SOX 404 — audit trail of changes made during approval
redFlags: Material amount or GL changes made by the approver in the same action as the approval
Mileage entered without a business purpose or destination
Edits made after an earlier tier already approved, with no re-routing
scr_ap_viewing_and_editing_transactions_.yardi: Yardi Voyager: opening a payable from the workflow queue in edit mode, then approving; changes captured in the payable's audit trail.

scr_ap_viewing_and_editing_transactions_.purpose: The same view-and-edit path described for a second Approval Workbench context, where the approver reviews a queued transaction, adjusts fields such as expense category and amount, saves, and then records the approve or decline decision.
scr_ap_viewing_and_editing_transactions_.outcome: The reviewed transaction carries the approver's corrections and a decision, and moves either to the next tier or back to the submitter.
scr_ap_viewing_and_editing_transactions_.rootCause: Once a journal entry has passed approval it can no longer be edited, so this screen is the last point at which coding can be fixed without a reversing entry. Reviewers who let an item through intending to correct it later find themselves writing a reclass in the following period, which shows up in the owner's operating statement as a prior-period adjustment nobody asked for.
scr_ap_viewing_and_editing_transactions_.ifSkipped: Coding errors survive approval and must be unwound with reclassification entries that clutter the trial balance and invite owner questions.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 12, controls performed at the point they are effective
ASC 250-10 — correction of an error versus a change in estimate
SOX 404 — approval evidence tied to the final version of the record
redFlags: Approvals granted on the understanding that accounting will fix the coding afterwards
Reclass volume rising month over month in the same expense accounts
Journal entries approved and then found to need correction, forcing a reversal
scr_ap_viewing_and_editing_transactions_.yardi: Yardi Voyager: payable or journal entry opened from the approval queue; post-approval changes require a reversing entry.

scr_ap_viewing_and_editing_transactions_.purpose: A third Approval Workbench entry point for the view, edit and decide sequence, reached from a different navigation path but governing the same in-queue editing behavior across transaction types.
scr_ap_viewing_and_editing_transactions_.outcome: The approver disposes of the item from wherever they entered the workbench, with the same edit rights and the same post-approval lock on journal entries.
scr_ap_viewing_and_editing_transactions_.rootCause: Having several routes into the same editing capability means access is granted several times over, and permission reviews that check one path miss the others. A user restricted from editing invoices in the A/P module may still reach the same edit form through a workbench path, which is how an access review signs off clean on a right that is actually open.
scr_ap_viewing_and_editing_transactions_.ifSkipped: Approvers cannot correct items from the entry point they actually use, so they bounce transactions back and the approval cycle lengthens.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 11, controls over technology access
SOC 1 — logical access consistency across entry points
SOX 404 — completeness of the user access review
redFlags: Edit rights available through a workbench path that the access review did not test
Different approval behavior depending on which menu the user came from
Roles granted workbench access broadly to avoid support tickets
scr_ap_viewing_and_editing_transactions_.yardi: Yardi Voyager: the same payable edit form reachable from the workflow queue and from Payables > Payable Entry, governed by separate menu rights.

scr_ap_available_budget_page.purpose: Opens from the Spend control button on an A/P invoice, purchase order or subcontract and shows budget, actual and remaining for the property and account — with Month, Year to date and Current Year tabs for standard line entry, or job cost code figures when the line entry type is Job Cost.
scr_ap_available_budget_page.outcome: The person coding or approving the transaction sees, before committing, whether the account has budget left for the month, the year to date and the remainder of the year.
scr_ap_available_budget_page.rootCause: The three tabs answer three different questions and choosing the wrong one produces false comfort. An account with room in the Current Year tab can be fully consumed for the month, and approving against annual headroom is how a property burns its whole R&M budget by August. On job cost lines the remaining figure ignores open commitments unless the PO was entered, so uncommitted work looks affordable when it is not.
scr_ap_available_budget_page.ifSkipped: Spend is approved with no visibility of remaining budget, and the overrun surfaces in the monthly variance package weeks after the money is committed.
gaap: Loan agreement approved-budget covenants
Partnership agreement major-decision thresholds
COSO 2013 — Principle 16, ongoing monitoring against plan
redFlags: Approvals justified by Current Year headroom while the Month tab is already overspent
Job cost remaining balances that exclude open commitments
The budget shown being a working version rather than the owner-approved one
scr_ap_available_budget_page.yardi: Yardi Voyager: budget check on the payable or PO against Financials > Budget, with job cost budget comparison in Job Cost.

scr_ap_approval_history_list.purpose: Opens from a status link in the workbench and lays out a transaction's full approval trail — each policy type and policy name the system applied, who acted at each level, and when — including the default policy and workflow that RealPage auto-generates and shows only to admin users.
scr_ap_approval_history_list.outcome: A single retrievable record showing that the right approvers, at the right levels, authorized the transaction before it posted.
scr_ap_approval_history_list.rootCause: Auditors do not accept 'the system requires approval' as evidence; they select invoices and ask to see who approved each one. The auto-generated default policy is the exposure here — because it is invisible to non-admin users, an item that routed through it looks approved in the history while nobody outside IT can explain which human authority it represented.
scr_ap_approval_history_list.ifSkipped: There is no retrievable proof of who authorized a given disbursement, and the authorization control is deemed ineffective regardless of how it was configured.
gaap: SOX 404 — evidence of operating effectiveness, not just design
18 U.S.C. §1519 (SOX §802) — audit records must not be altered or destroyed
AU-C 240 — evaluating management override
redFlags: Transactions whose only approval came from the auto-generated default policy
Approval timestamps clustered within seconds across dozens of invoices
History showing a level skipped with no submitter-level explanation
scr_ap_approval_history_list.yardi: Yardi Voyager: the workflow history on each payable plus Administration > User Activity / change log reports.

scr_ap_review_and_approve_process_for_a_.purpose: Describes the accelerated A/P-invoice-only review mode that advances straight to the next invoice in the queue instead of returning to the workbench between items, paired with the image viewer so the invoice document opens alongside the coding.
scr_ap_review_and_approve_process_for_a_.outcome: An approver clears a queue of invoices in one continuous pass, with each invoice's scanned document visible next to the amounts being approved.
scr_ap_review_and_approve_process_for_a_.rootCause: Speed is the whole point of this mode and also its risk. Without the image viewer configured, an approver is clicking through amounts and GL codes with no source document in front of them — approving that a number exists, not that the property received the goods. The process also requires a reviewer policy type and a workflow assignment before it appears, so portfolios often turn on the fast path without the accounting-reviewer control that was supposed to sit in front of it.
scr_ap_review_and_approve_process_for_a_.ifSkipped: Approvers open each invoice individually and return to the workbench between items, which on a 200-invoice week pushes approvals past the check-run cut-off.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 10, approval supported by underlying documentation
IRC §6001 and Treas. Reg. §1.6001-1 — retrievable source documents
SOX 404 — approval based on sufficient information
redFlags: Fast review enabled without the image viewer, so approvals happen document-blind
Reviewer policy type never created, leaving the accounting review tier missing
Approval rates of several invoices per minute sustained across a queue
scr_ap_review_and_approve_process_for_a_.yardi: Yardi Voyager: PAYscan invoice register review with the scanned image pane, advancing through the workflow queue.

scr_ap_viewing_approval_policy_details_f.purpose: Drills from the Policy name column in a transaction's approval history into the Approval Policy Manager, exposing the thresholds, tiers and assigned roles of the policy that actually decided the item, with a Print option for the work papers.
scr_ap_viewing_approval_policy_details_f.outcome: The reviewer can prove not just who approved a transaction but that the policy which routed it carried the correct dollar limits and approver assignments.
scr_ap_viewing_approval_policy_details_f.rootCause: Policies get edited. An invoice approved in March under a $5,000 limit may today sit under a policy showing $25,000, and this drill-through shows the current policy, not a snapshot of the one in force on the approval date. An auditor testing a March sample needs that distinction made explicit, or the work paper quietly asserts a control that did not exist at the time.
scr_ap_viewing_approval_policy_details_f.ifSkipped: The approval history names an approver and a policy but nobody can show what authority that policy conferred, leaving the control untestable.
gaap: SOX 404 — testing the authorization control against its design at the transaction date
COSO 2013 — Principle 10, documented limits of authority
SOC 1 — control description supported by configuration evidence
reports: Printed policy detail for work papers
redFlags: Policy thresholds changed mid-period with no change log filed
Printed policy evidence dated after the period being tested
Policies with an approver role that no longer maps to any active user
scr_ap_viewing_approval_policy_details_f.yardi: Yardi Voyager: the workflow definition behind an approval step, viewed from Administration > Workflow setup while tracing a payable.

scr_ap_viewing_workflow_details_from_app.purpose: Opens the Workflow name link inside a transaction's approval history to show the workflow that routed it — the ordered policies it contained, any override flags, and the entities it was assigned to — printable for audit evidence.
scr_ap_viewing_workflow_details_from_app.outcome: The routing path a transaction actually took is reconstructable end to end, from entity assignment through each policy in sequence.
scr_ap_viewing_workflow_details_from_app.rootCause: Workflows carry override flags, and an overriding policy short-circuits the tiers below it. Reading only the approval history, an item that took one signature looks under-approved; opening the workflow shows the override that legitimately collapsed the path — or shows that no override existed and the item genuinely skipped a level. Without this drill-through a reviewer cannot tell a designed shortcut from a control failure.
scr_ap_viewing_workflow_details_from_app.ifSkipped: Single-signature approvals on large items cannot be explained, and the reviewer either raises a false exception or misses a real one.
gaap: SOX 404 — evidencing the complete routing path of an approved transaction
COSO 2013 — Principle 10, override mechanisms documented and justified
18 U.S.C. §1519 — workflow evidence retained intact
reports: Printed workflow detail for work papers
redFlags: Override policies in workflows covering high-value transaction types
Workflows assigned to entities that no longer exist in the portfolio
An entity matching no workflow, so its transactions post unrouted
scr_ap_viewing_workflow_details_from_app.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Administration > Workflow setup showing the step sequence and property assignment behind a payable's approval.

scr_ap_enabling_the_image_viewer.purpose: A per-user preference under My preferences > Display > Personalize interactive behavior that opens invoice attachments in a separate window, so the scanned document and the coding screen are visible at the same time during review and approve.
scr_ap_enabling_the_image_viewer.outcome: Each approver who enables it reviews invoices against the actual vendor document instead of against keyed fields alone.
scr_ap_enabling_the_image_viewer.rootCause: Because it lives in personal preferences, there is no way to require it. The portfolio can mandate that approvers verify the invoice image and still have half of them approving from the data-entry screen with the attachment unopened — which is how a keying error of a transposed amount, or an invoice for the wrong property, gets approved by someone who never looked at the paper. A three-way match on screen values alone matches nothing.
scr_ap_enabling_the_image_viewer.ifSkipped: Attachments open in the same window and interrupt the review flow, so approvers stop opening them and effectively approve on keyed data only.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 13, relevant information to support the control
IRC §6001 — source documents supporting the deduction
SOX 404 — approval based on examination of supporting evidence
reports: A/P invoice register with attachment flag
redFlags: Approvers with the preference off approving high-value invoices
Invoices approved where no attachment exists at all
Keyed amount differing from the attached document on a sample check
scr_ap_enabling_the_image_viewer.yardi: Yardi Voyager: PAYscan image pane displayed alongside the invoice register entry during workflow review.

scr_ap_adding_a_reviewer_policy_to_a_wor.purpose: Attaches an accounting-reviewer policy to an existing approval workflow from Company > All > Approval Workflow, adding it as a row in the Policies list and optionally flagging it as an override, then assigning the workflow to the properties it governs.
scr_ap_adding_a_reviewer_policy_to_a_wor.outcome: A/P invoices for the assigned properties pass an accounting review tier before or alongside operational approval, unlocking the Review & approve fast path.
scr_ap_adding_a_reviewer_policy_to_a_wor.rootCause: The Override check box on this row is the part that gets clicked without thought. Marking the accounting reviewer as an override means the reviewer's sign-off replaces the operational approvals beneath it — the accountant confirming GL coding is suddenly also confirming that the work was performed, which they have no way to know. That is an operational control silently reassigned to someone sitting in another country.
scr_ap_adding_a_reviewer_policy_to_a_wor.ifSkipped: The reviewer policy exists but governs nothing, the Review & approve button never appears, and invoices route with no accounting review of coding at all.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 10, layered review with distinct responsibilities
SOX 404 — reviewer competence matched to what is being attested
SOC 1 — service organization control boundaries where review is offshore
redFlags: Override selected on the reviewer policy, collapsing operational approval into accounting review
Reviewer policy added to the workflow but no property assigned
Reviewer tier populated by the same offshore team that enters the invoices
scr_ap_adding_a_reviewer_policy_to_a_wor.yardi: Yardi Voyager: adding an accounting-review step to a PAYscan workflow and assigning it to the property set.

scr_ap_reviewing_and_approving_a_p_invoi.purpose: The Review & approve run itself — filter the workbench to A/P invoices, click Review & approve, and work the queue with Approve & next, or skip an invoice with Next, while the image viewer shows the document; approved eInvoices also push a Pending-to-Approved status update back to the vendor through OpsMerchant.
scr_ap_reviewing_and_approving_a_p_invoi.outcome: The queue is cleared invoice by invoice, edits made during review are saved and routed onward, and eInvoice vendors see their status change without an email from A/P.
scr_ap_reviewing_and_approving_a_p_invoi.rootCause: Skip is the quiet problem. An invoice passed over with Next leaves no decline, no comment and no trace of hesitation — it simply returns to the bottom of the queue, and the disputed or on-hold item that the approver was uneasy about circles indefinitely while the vendor's aging climbs. The OpsMerchant status push compounds it: the vendor gets a definitive Approved signal from a fast-path click and starts expecting payment on terms.
scr_ap_reviewing_and_approving_a_p_invoi.ifSkipped: Approvers cannot process a large invoice queue at the pace the check-run calendar requires, and invoices miss the payment cut-off or the accrual cut-off.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 10, documented disposition of every item reviewed
ASC 405-10 — the liability is recognized when approved and posted
SOX 404 — evidence that the approval was an informed decision
redFlags: Invoices skipped with Next more than twice and never declined or escalated
eInvoices marked Approved to the vendor while still on internal hold
Bulk approvals completed faster than the invoices could have been read
scr_ap_reviewing_and_approving_a_p_invoi.yardi: Yardi Voyager: PAYscan workflow queue processed sequentially, with vendor-facing status via VendorCafe.

scr_ap_creating_a_reviewer_policy_type.purpose: Creates a policy in the Approval Policy Manager using the Accounting reviewer policy type — naming it, setting its status, and assigning either a role with up to four review levels or individual users one level deep, which is the prerequisite for the whole Review & approve process.
scr_ap_creating_a_reviewer_policy_type.outcome: An accounting review tier exists that can be attached to workflows, giving A/P invoices a coding-and-documentation check distinct from operational approval.
scr_ap_creating_a_reviewer_policy_type.rootCause: The role-versus-user choice here quietly decides how resilient the control is. Naming individual users caps the policy at one level of review and breaks the moment someone leaves or takes leave; naming a role supports up to four levels and survives staff turnover. Portfolios choose users because it is faster to set up, then spend the next year editing the policy every time the offshore team rotates.
scr_ap_creating_a_reviewer_policy_type.ifSkipped: There is no accounting reviewer tier to attach to workflows, the Review & approve button never becomes available, and coding review happens informally or not at all.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 10, review controls defined by role rather than individual
SOX 404 — control continuity across personnel changes
SOC 1 — documented review responsibilities in the delivery model
redFlags: Reviewer policies naming individual users, which break on turnover and allow only one level
Policy created with an Inactive status and never enabled
Four review levels configured where only one person actually reviews
scr_ap_creating_a_reviewer_policy_type.yardi: Yardi Voyager: defining an accounting-review workflow step by role in Administration > Workflow setup.

scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_overview.purpose: The conceptual grounding for vendor records — a vendor supplies goods or services, the company issues a purchase order, the vendor delivers and invoices, and the three documents are matched before payment, with every vendor requiring a record before any of that can happen.
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_overview.outcome: Staff understand that the vendor record is the gate, and that three-way matching depends on the PO, receipt and invoice all referencing the same vendor record.
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_overview.rootCause: The vendor master is the highest-value fraud target in the entire A/P system: whoever controls it controls where the money goes. The overview establishes that adding a vendor is a controlled act requiring W-9, remit-to address, payment method and optional approval — not a data-entry convenience a site manager performs to get an invoice paid this afternoon.
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_overview.ifSkipped: Vendors are created ad hoc to clear individual invoices, duplicates proliferate, and the three-way match has nothing stable to match against.
gaap: IRC §6109 — TIN collection before payment
31 CFR Part 501 — OFAC screening of counterparties
COSO 2013 — Principle 10, vendor master change controls
redFlags: Vendors created without a W-9 on file
Vendor records added by the same person who enters that vendor's invoices
Vendor names that closely mirror an existing vendor with a different remit-to address
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_overview.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Vendor master, with VendorCafe for self-service onboarding and compliance documents.

scr_ap_vendor_record_approval_process.purpose: Walks the optional vendor-record approval cycle end to end — requester creates or updates a vendor, the policy decides whether approval is required, approvers are notified by email and work the Approve vendors list, and approved records join the vendor master while declined ones return to the requester.
scr_ap_vendor_record_approval_process.outcome: New and changed vendor records are authorized by someone other than the requester before they can receive a payment.
scr_ap_vendor_record_approval_process.rootCause: This process is the only structural defense against payment-diversion fraud, which almost never involves a fake invoice — it involves a real vendor whose bank details were changed. If the policy covers new vendors but not updates, the control misses the exact event it exists to catch, and the approver clicking through an email link sees a bank account they have no independent way to verify.
scr_ap_vendor_record_approval_process.ifSkipped: Anyone who can create a vendor can direct a payment, and a changed remit-to or ACH detail reaches the payment run with no second pair of eyes.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 10, segregation of vendor master maintenance from payment
31 CFR Part 501 — OFAC screening before the vendor becomes payable
IRC §6109 — valid TIN captured before the first payment
redFlags: Approval policy covering new vendors but exempting updates to existing ones
Bank detail changes approved from the email link without an independent call-back
Requester and approver being the same individual under a shared login
scr_ap_vendor_record_approval_process.yardi: Yardi Voyager: vendor approval workflow in Administration > Workflow setup, with the vendor held in pending status until approved.

scr_ap_vendor_remittance_emails.purpose: Explains the automated remittance notification RealPage sends a vendor when a payment is made — full, partial, or full payment applied from a credit — and the setup it depends on: remittance email addresses and attachment format on each vendor record.
scr_ap_vendor_remittance_emails.outcome: Vendors receive machine-generated remittance detail showing which invoices a payment settled, cutting the volume of 'what was this check for' calls into the A/P team.
scr_ap_vendor_remittance_emails.rootCause: Remittance advices are how vendors apply cash, and a wrong one causes the property's own aging to diverge from the vendor's statement. The partial-payment and credit-applied cases are where it bites: a vendor who receives a remittance for a credit application with no cash behind it frequently posts it as a payment, leaving both ledgers out of step until someone reconciles a year of activity line by line.
scr_ap_vendor_remittance_emails.ifSkipped: Vendors misapply payments, statements disagree with the A/P aging, and the offshore team spends the close week reconciling vendor statements by hand.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 14, external communication supporting the control
ASC 405-10 — accurate derecognition of the liability
SOC 1 — vendor-identifying data leaving the system boundary
redFlags: Remittance emails going to a stale address after the vendor's contact changed
Credit-applied remittances mistaken by vendors for cash payments
Remittance detail sent before the payment is actually released
scr_ap_vendor_remittance_emails.yardi: Yardi Voyager: emailed remittance advice from check or EFT processing, configured on the vendor's payment settings.

scr_ap_vendor_supplier_information_page.purpose: The multi-tab vendor record itself — Vendor (Supplier) with its Summary and Primary contact sections, Additional information carrying vendor details, billing details, email template options, vendor merge and CA DE 542, plus the contact, payment, owner, 1099 and restrictions tabs.
scr_ap_vendor_supplier_information_page.outcome: One record holds every attribute that drives how a vendor is coded, paid, restricted and reported, and the tabs make each attribute reviewable in isolation.
scr_ap_vendor_supplier_information_page.rootCause: The information that matters most for control is scattered across tabs a reviewer will not open unless prompted: the 1099 flag on one, the payment method and remit-to on another, the restrictions on a third that is only visible at the top level of a multi-entity company. A vendor reviewed by scanning the first tab looks complete while the tax and payment attributes behind it are blank or wrong.
scr_ap_vendor_supplier_information_page.ifSkipped: Vendor attributes are set inconsistently, invoices default to the wrong GL group, and 1099 or payment configuration is discovered missing at year-end or at the check run.
gaap: IRC §6041 — reportable payment attributes captured on the master record
IRC §6109 — TIN recorded and matched
COSO 2013 — Principle 13, complete and accurate master data
redFlags: Vendor records saved with only the first tab completed
Payment information tab left blank on vendors already receiving checks
GL group missing, so every invoice for the vendor must be coded from scratch
scr_ap_vendor_supplier_information_page.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Vendor with its Vendor, Attributes, Insurance and 1099 tabs.

scr_ap_form_1099_information_page.purpose: Sets the vendor's Form 1099 designation and line items — selecting a form populates the eligible boxes and adds a Form 1099 section to the A/P invoice page so amounts can be allocated across 1099 accounts; choosing None excludes the vendor, and multi-entity companies issuing separate 1099s per entity select the entity for initial YTD amounts.
scr_ap_form_1099_information_page.outcome: Payments accumulate into the correct form and box automatically, and prior-system YTD amounts are seeded so a mid-year conversion still produces a complete 1099.
scr_ap_form_1099_information_page.rootCause: The initial YTD field is the one that ruins Januarys. A portfolio that converts to RealPage in July and leaves it blank issues 1099s covering half a year of payments to every contractor, and the mismatch surfaces when vendors compare the form against their own books. The per-entity selection matters just as much: issuing one combined 1099 where the owner structure requires separate filings per entity puts the wrong payer TIN on the form.
scr_ap_form_1099_information_page.ifSkipped: Reportable vendors accumulate no 1099 totals, or totals cover only the post-conversion period, and January filing requires reconstructing payments from the check register.
gaap: IRC §6041 / §6041A — information returns for services and rents
IRC §6721 / §6722 — per-form penalties for late or incorrect filings
IRC §3406 — 24% backup withholding where the TIN is missing or wrong
redFlags: Mid-year conversions with no initial YTD amounts entered
Attorneys set to None because the firm is incorporated
Multi-entity companies issuing combined 1099s where separate payer TINs are required
scr_ap_form_1099_information_page.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > 1099 Processing driven by the vendor's 1099 category and box, with 1099 adjustment entries for prior-system amounts.

scr_ap_using_the_de_542_form_for_a_vendo.purpose: Covers California's DE 542 independent contractor reporting — the state requires a service-recipient to report specified information about each service-provider — including setting the vendor up for DE 542 and printing the data as a report or form, with RealPage Support handling installation.
scr_ap_using_the_de_542_form_for_a_vendo.outcome: California properties capture and file contractor information within the state's reporting window, separately from federal 1099 reporting.
scr_ap_using_the_de_542_form_for_a_vendo.rootCause: DE 542 is a state obligation on a much tighter clock than the 1099 — California requires reporting within 20 days of reaching $600 or entering the contract, whichever is earlier, not in January. Portfolios that treat it as a year-end task are late on every contractor. The data also feeds child-support enforcement, so the state pursues non-filers rather than ignoring them.
scr_ap_using_the_de_542_form_for_a_vendo.ifSkipped: California properties miss the 20-day reporting window on every independent contractor, exposing the owner to per-failure state penalties.
gaap: California Unemployment Insurance Code §1088.8 — DE 542 independent contractor reporting
IRC §6041A — parallel federal reporting on the same payments
COSO 2013 — Principle 12, controls over jurisdiction-specific filings
reports: Vendor master list filtered to California
redFlags: California vendors with no DE 542 flag set
DE 542 treated as an annual rather than a rolling 20-day obligation
Sent-date field left blank so nobody can prove the filing was made
scr_ap_using_the_de_542_form_for_a_vendo.yardi: Yardi Voyager: state contractor reporting handled through custom vendor attributes and a DE 542 extract report.

scr_ap_merging_vendors.purpose: Consolidates duplicate vendor records by comparing two side by side, confirming they are the same party, and repointing linked transactions to the surviving record while the second becomes inactive — with the warning that invoices left out force reactivating the inactive record and repeating the merge.
scr_ap_merging_vendors.outcome: One vendor record carries the complete payment and invoice history, and the duplicate is retired without orphaning any transaction.
scr_ap_merging_vendors.rootCause: Duplicate vendors are how a portfolio pays the same invoice twice and never notices: the duplicate-invoice-number check runs per vendor, so the identical invoice entered under 'ABC Plumbing' and 'ABC Plumbing Inc' passes cleanly. Duplicates also split the year's payments across two records, so each falls under the $600 threshold and neither triggers a 1099. The merge fixes both, but only if every transaction is swept in.
scr_ap_merging_vendors.ifSkipped: Payment history stays split, the duplicate-invoice control keeps failing between the two records, and 1099 totals understate what the vendor was actually paid.
gaap: IRC §6041 — aggregate payments to one payee determine reportability
COSO 2013 — Principle 10, duplicate payment prevention
IRC §6001 — merged history retained, not deleted
redFlags: Merges done without confirming both records share the same TIN
Invoices omitted from the merge, requiring reactivation and a second attempt
Duplicate vendors left unmerged through year-end, splitting 1099 totals below the threshold
scr_ap_merging_vendors.yardi: Yardi Voyager: vendor merge utility repointing payables and checks to the surviving vendor code.

scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_list.purpose: The working vendor list reached from Search & Find, where vendors are added, viewed, edited and deleted, the A/P ledger and total due are opened per vendor, and vendor information is exported — with a View due link replacing the amount in multi-entity, multi-base-currency companies.
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_list.outcome: The A/P team works from one list that surfaces each vendor's open balance and links straight into their ledger, without running a report first.
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_list.rootCause: The Total due figure on this list is the number people quote when an owner asks what a vendor is owed, and in a multi-entity company it is not a number at all — it is a link, because the balance spans entities in different base currencies. Reading a single-entity habit into a multi-entity list, or exporting the column and summing it, produces a vendor exposure figure that is wrong in a way nobody catches until the owner's counsel asks about a specific contract.
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_list.ifSkipped: Vendor balances are looked up one report at a time, and the team loses the fastest route from a vendor question to that vendor's ledger.
gaap: ASC 405-10 — liability balances by counterparty
COSO 2013 — Principle 13, accurate information for decision-making
ASC 830 — balances held in different functional currencies
redFlags: Total due read as a single figure in a multi-entity, multi-currency company
Vendor list exported with inactive and one-time vendors silently excluded
Delete used on a vendor with transaction history instead of inactivation
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_list.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Vendor search list with the open balance column and drill-through to the vendor ledger.

scr_ap_example_of_vendors_list.purpose: A worked illustration of the vendor list and its filters — Include One-time to surface vendors flagged for single use, Include Inactive to reveal retired vendors still linked to transactions, group filters built on vendor dimension groups, and the hierarchical parent-child display shown with icons and indentation.
scr_ap_example_of_vendors_list.outcome: Users understand that the default list is a filtered subset and know which switch reveals the vendors it is hiding.
scr_ap_example_of_vendors_list.rootCause: Every one of these filters defaults to hiding something, and the hidden rows are exactly the ones that matter at close. Inactive vendors are inactive precisely because they still carry history — an accountant tying 2010 Accounts Payable to the vendor aging and working from the default list will find a variance they cannot explain, because the inactive vendor with a residual balance is not on the page. One-time vendors, the highest-risk category in the whole master file, are hidden by the same default.
scr_ap_example_of_vendors_list.ifSkipped: Staff take the default list as the complete vendor population and reconcile, review and audit against a filtered subset without knowing it.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 13, completeness of information used in a control
ASC 405-10 — completeness of the liability population
SOX 404 — reconciliation performed over the full population
redFlags: A/P control account tie-outs run against the default filtered vendor list
One-time vendors never reviewed because they are hidden by default
Parent-child hierarchy hiding a subsidiary vendor's balance under a collapsed parent
scr_ap_example_of_vendors_list.yardi: Yardi Voyager: vendor search filters for active status and vendor type, with parent vendor relationships shown on the vendor record.

scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_additional_info.purpose: The Additional Information tab where the vendor's Type ID grouping, parent vendor, G/L group or account label, Tax ID (EIN), 1099 eligibility and 1099 name are set, alongside documents, special designation, vendor merge and CA DE 542 sections.
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_additional_info.outcome: The vendor carries the coding defaults and tax identity that drive every invoice entered against it and every 1099 produced for it.
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_additional_info.rootCause: The G/L group set here becomes the default coding on every future invoice for the vendor, and defaults are accepted, not reviewed. A landscaping vendor pointed at 6110 Repairs & Maintenance will have its irrigation system replacement — a capital item belonging in 1530 Building Improvements — expensed by default, month after month, until a fixed-asset review catches it. The 1099 name field is separate from the vendor name for a reason: the IRS matches on the legal name, and 'Mike's Handyman Service' will not TIN-match against Michael Ortega's SSN.
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_additional_info.ifSkipped: Invoices default to no GL account and are coded ad hoc, and the vendor's EIN and 1099 name are missing when the year-end run needs them.
gaap: IRC §6109 — EIN or SSN recorded before payment
IRC §6041 — 1099 eligibility and legal name for the information return
Treas. Reg. §1.263(a)-3 — default coding must not pre-decide capital versus repair
redFlags: 1099 name left as the trade name rather than the legal name on the W-9
G/L group pointing at an expense account for vendors who routinely perform capital work
1099 eligible unchecked on unincorporated service vendors
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_additional_info.yardi: Yardi Voyager: vendor Attributes tab carrying default expense account, vendor type, tax ID and 1099 category.

scr_ap_defining_a_vendors_special_design.purpose: Flags a vendor as women-owned, veteran-owned, HUBZone or 8(a) socially and economically disadvantaged on the Additional Information tab, with an expiration date per designation — the status expires after nine years of holding it.
scr_ap_defining_a_vendors_special_design.outcome: Diverse-supplier spend can be identified and reported by designation, with expired certifications distinguishable from current ones.
scr_ap_defining_a_vendors_special_design.rootCause: Supplier-diversity spend is reported to institutional owners, HUD and state housing agencies as a percentage of total procurement, and the number is only as good as the expiration dates. A designation flagged once and never dated keeps counting a vendor as diverse years after its certification lapsed, which overstates the figure in an owner report — and on HUD or agency-financed properties an overstated diversity claim is a representation to a government funder, not just an internal metric.
scr_ap_defining_a_vendors_special_design.ifSkipped: Diverse-supplier spend cannot be reported, and the property fails the supplier-diversity reporting its owner or agency lender requires.
gaap: HUD and state agency supplier-diversity reporting requirements
COSO 2013 — Principle 13, accuracy of reported non-financial information
Management agreement reporting covenants
redFlags: Designations flagged with no expiration date recorded
Certifications past the nine-year limit still counting toward diversity spend
Designation set from a vendor's claim with no certificate on file
scr_ap_defining_a_vendors_special_design.yardi: Yardi Voyager: vendor attribute or user-defined field flagging diversity classification with a certification expiry date.

scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_contact_list_ta.purpose: The Contact List tab holding every contact for a vendor and the Pay to / Return to assignments — the Pay to contact becomes the default for printing checks and creating A/P invoices, Return to is used across several A/P activities, and a dedicated 1099 contact can be named for printing.
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_contact_list_ta.outcome: Payments, correspondence and 1099 forms each route to the contact the vendor designated for that purpose rather than to one generic address.
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_contact_list_ta.rootCause: The Pay to contact carries the address a check is physically mailed to, which makes this tab a payment-control surface disguised as a contact list. Adding a new contact and selecting it as Pay to redirects every future check for that vendor, and it is a far quieter change than editing the primary address — no address-change review will look here. Anyone able to edit contacts can effectively change where the money goes.
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_contact_list_ta.ifSkipped: Checks and 1099s go to a general office address, get lost internally at the vendor, and the A/P team fields calls about payments the vendor says it never received.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 10, controls over payment destination changes
IRC §6041 — 1099 delivered to the payee by January 31
SOC 1 — change control over remittance data
redFlags: Pay to contact changed without the same verification applied to a remit-to address change
A new contact added and immediately set as Pay to by the person entering that vendor's invoices
1099 contact pointing at a person who left the vendor
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_contact_list_ta.yardi: Yardi Voyager: vendor contacts with separate remit-to and 1099 addresses on the vendor record.

scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_owner_informati.purpose: The Owner Information tab, which appears only when the vendor is an owner of the company, used to classify owner payments — selecting the default equity account for the owner and setting Hold distribution to postpone paying them.
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_owner_informati.outcome: Owner payments are classified against the equity structure rather than as operating expense, and distributions can be suspended without inactivating the vendor.
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_owner_informati.rootCause: An owner paid as a vendor is a related-party transaction, and if it routes through the default expense coding the distribution lands in operating expense — inflating expenses, depressing NOI, and misstating the capital accounts that drive the waterfall. The Hold distribution flag matters just as much: distributions are frequently blocked by a loan covenant or a DSCR test, and this checkbox is the mechanical enforcement of a decision the lender made.
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_owner_informati.ifSkipped: Owner distributions post as operating expense, NOI is understated, partner capital accounts are wrong, and related-party disclosure is incomplete.
gaap: ASC 850 — related-party transactions and disclosure
ASC 505-10 — equity distributions versus expense
Loan agreement distribution restrictions and DSCR tests
redFlags: Owner-vendor records with no default equity account, defaulting distributions to expense
Hold distribution cleared without evidence the covenant test was passed
Owner payments absent from the related-party disclosure schedule
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_owner_informati.yardi: Yardi Voyager: owner/investor payments handled through the Investment Management distribution module rather than as trade payables.

scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_restrictions_ta.purpose: The Restrictions tab, accessible only at the top level of a multi-entity shared environment, limiting a vendor to all locations, top level only, or a selected set of locations, location groups, departments and department groups.
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_restrictions_ta.outcome: A vendor appears only where it is authorized to be used, so site staff cannot code an invoice to a property the vendor is not approved to serve.
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_restrictions_ta.rootCause: Restrictions are how a shared vendor master serves a portfolio with different owners: a vendor engaged under one owner's master service agreement, at that owner's negotiated rate, must not be selectable at a property owned by someone else. Leaving vendors unrestricted lets a property inherit pricing and insurance terms that were never negotiated on its behalf — and on properties with separate insurance requirements, engages a contractor whose certificate of insurance does not name that owner as additional insured.
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_restrictions_ta.ifSkipped: Every vendor is selectable at every property, cross-owner contract terms are applied where they do not belong, and insurance compliance cannot be enforced by property.
gaap: ASC 850 — transactions routed across entities under common control
COSO 2013 — Principle 10, access limited to authorized combinations
Management agreement scope-of-authority provisions
reports: Vendor master list with restriction status
redFlags: Master-service-agreement vendors left unrestricted across a mixed-owner portfolio
Restrictions maintained at the entity level where only top level has effect
Vendors restricted after they already carry active accounts at excluded locations
scr_ap_vendors_suppliers_restrictions_ta.yardi: Yardi Voyager: vendor property-scope restrictions controlling which properties may select the vendor on a payable.

scr_ap_setting_up_vendor_restrictions.purpose: The procedure for applying those restrictions — going to the top level of the company, opening the vendor from Accounts Payable > Vendors, using the Restrictions tab and choosing Unrestricted, Restricted to top-level only, or a selected location list before saving.
scr_ap_setting_up_vendor_restrictions.outcome: The vendor's availability matches the properties it is contracted to serve, enforced at entry rather than caught in review.
scr_ap_setting_up_vendor_restrictions.rootCause: The top-level requirement defeats the people best placed to know the answer. A regional accountant working inside an entity cannot set restrictions at all and has no indication the tab exists, so restriction setup falls to a system administrator who does not know which vendors serve which properties. The result is a portfolio where restrictions are configured for whichever vendors someone happened to raise a ticket about.
scr_ap_setting_up_vendor_restrictions.ifSkipped: Restrictions are never applied because nobody at entity level can reach the tab, and the vendor master stays wide open across the portfolio.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 11, access controls configured by someone with the knowledge to set them
SOC 1 — segregation between configuration and operation
Management agreement scope-of-authority provisions
reports: Vendor master list with restriction status
redFlags: Restrictions set only for vendors that generated a support ticket
Top-level access granted broadly so entity staff can set restrictions themselves
Restriction changes made with no record of who requested them or why
scr_ap_setting_up_vendor_restrictions.yardi: Yardi Voyager: vendor property scope maintained centrally, since property-level users cannot alter the shared vendor master.

scr_ap_marking_a_vendor_as_dont_pay.purpose: Sets the Don't pay flag in the Billing details section of a vendor's Additional Information tab, used when the company has ended the relationship — over quality, unresolved disputes or the vendor going out of business — and intends to make no further payments.
scr_ap_marking_a_vendor_as_dont_pay.outcome: The vendor is blocked from payment selection while its record and history remain intact for reference and reporting.
scr_ap_marking_a_vendor_as_dont_pay.rootCause: Don't pay stops the disbursement; it does not extinguish the obligation. Invoices for work genuinely performed stay in 2010 Accounts Payable and keep aging, and the accountant who assumes the flag resolved the matter leaves a liability on the balance sheet indefinitely. Where the vendor has gone out of business the balance eventually becomes unclaimed property owed to the state under escheat rules, not a windfall the property can write off to income.
scr_ap_marking_a_vendor_as_dont_pay.ifSkipped: A disputed or terminated vendor stays in the payment population and the next check run pays exactly the invoices the company decided to withhold.
gaap: ASC 450-20 — loss contingencies where the dispute is unresolved
ASC 405-20 — derecognition of a liability only when legally released
State unclaimed property (escheat) statutes for balances owed to unreachable vendors
redFlags: Don't pay vendors carrying aged balances with no contingency assessment
Old payables to defunct vendors written off to income instead of escheated
The flag set without documenting the dispute or the decision behind it
scr_ap_marking_a_vendor_as_dont_pay.yardi: Yardi Voyager: vendor hold flag suppressing the vendor from check processing while open payables remain on the aging.

scr_ap_tips_for_adding_new_vendors.purpose: The practical checklist for adding vendors — work at the top level, supply the minimum columns of Vendor ID, Vendor Name and Print as, complete any required custom fields, and ideally include vendor account number, contact name, phone, email, URL and address.
scr_ap_tips_for_adding_new_vendors.outcome: New vendors enter the master with a unique ID, a payment-ready Print as name and enough contact detail to chase an invoice or a W-9.
scr_ap_tips_for_adding_new_vendors.rootCause: Print as is the field that actually appears on the check, and treating it as a formatting nicety produces a negotiable instrument the payee's bank will refuse. A check payable to 'ABC Plmb' does not match the account name at the vendor's bank and is returned; worse, a Print as holding a trade name where the vendor operates as a sole proprietor produces a check the individual cannot deposit and a 1099 that will not TIN-match.
scr_ap_tips_for_adding_new_vendors.ifSkipped: Vendors are created with inconsistent IDs and a Print as that does not match the payee's legal or banking name, and checks are returned or rejected.
gaap: UCC Article 3 — payee designation on a negotiable instrument
IRC §6109 — payee identity consistent with the TIN on file
COSO 2013 — Principle 13, accurate master data at the point of creation
redFlags: Print as abbreviated or truncated so the check does not match the bank account name
Vendor IDs reused from a deleted record
Required custom fields bypassed by creating the vendor through import
scr_ap_tips_for_adding_new_vendors.yardi: Yardi Voyager: vendor code and payee name conventions set on the vendor record, with the payee name driving check printing.

scr_ap_about_vendor_contact_information.purpose: Explains how the Primary contact on the Vendor tab supplies the default for everything unless overridden, and how assigning a contact on the Contact list tab to the Primary, Pay to, Return to or 1099 type makes it the new default for that specific area.
scr_ap_about_vendor_contact_information.outcome: Staff understand the override hierarchy, so a change to one contact type does not silently change where checks or 1099s go.
scr_ap_about_vendor_contact_information.rootCause: The cascade is invisible in the interface. Assigning a contact as Primary on the contact list overrides the address on the vendor tab everywhere it was still cascading, so a person updating a phone number can move the check address without touching a single payment field. This is also the mechanism through which a suggested contact name shared across vendors, employees, customers and users can tie an A/P payee to an employee record — the exact pattern a fictitious-vendor test is designed to detect.
scr_ap_about_vendor_contact_information.ifSkipped: Contact edits produce unintended changes to payment and 1099 addresses, and nobody can explain why a check went to a different place this month.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 10, controls over data that determines payment destination
AU-C 240 — fictitious vendor and employee-vendor overlap risk
IRC §6041 — payee address for information return delivery
redFlags: Contact type assignments changed as part of a routine detail update
A vendor contact sharing an address or bank detail with an employee record
Return to and Pay to pointing at different companies entirely
scr_ap_about_vendor_contact_information.yardi: Yardi Voyager: vendor address types (remit-to, ordering, 1099) each overriding the vendor's primary address for their own purpose.

scr_ap_viewing_vendor_supplier_records.purpose: The read-only path into a vendor record — open the Vendors (Suppliers) list, find the vendor and click View to inspect the record without edit rights, with Edit available separately for those who need to change it.
scr_ap_viewing_vendor_supplier_records.outcome: Staff who need vendor information for coding, chasing a payment or answering an owner question can see the record without holding the rights to change it.
scr_ap_viewing_vendor_supplier_records.rootCause: Separating View from Edit is what makes vendor-master segregation of duties possible at all: the site manager and the offshore accountant both need to see remit-to and payment terms, and neither should be able to change them. Portfolios that grant edit access because the view path is slightly less convenient hand vendor-master maintenance to a dozen people, and every one of them becomes a route for a payment-diversion change.
scr_ap_viewing_vendor_supplier_records.ifSkipped: Anyone needing vendor information is granted edit access, and the population able to change payment destinations grows well past the people who should have it.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 11, least-privilege access to master data
SOC 1 — logical access controls over the vendor master
SOX 404 — user access review over payment-relevant data
redFlags: Edit rights on the vendor master granted to site staff for read-only needs
Change log showing edits by users whose role should be view-only
No periodic review of who holds vendor edit permission
scr_ap_viewing_vendor_supplier_records.yardi: Yardi Voyager: vendor record opened read-only where the user's menu rights exclude vendor maintenance.

scr_ap_inviting_vendors_to_the_realpage_.purpose: Sends an existing vendor an invitation to join the RealPage Vendor Marketplace from the Invite Vendor button on their record, where properties across the RealPage base can find them by category and confirm compliance, at no subscription cost to the vendor.
scr_ap_inviting_vendors_to_the_realpage_.outcome: The vendor joins the marketplace, becomes discoverable to other properties, and their compliance documentation is maintained through the platform.
scr_ap_inviting_vendors_to_the_realpage_.rootCause: Marketplace compliance verification is a convenience, not a transfer of responsibility. A vendor showing as compliant in the marketplace may hold general liability coverage that does not name this specific owner as additional insured and does not meet this property's required limits — and if an uninsured contractor injures someone on site, the owner's policy absorbs it regardless of what the marketplace badge said. The invitation also sends property-management contact data outbound, which the SOC 1 boundary covers.
scr_ap_inviting_vendors_to_the_realpage_.ifSkipped: Vendor compliance documents are chased by email and stored in a shared drive, and expired certificates of insurance are noticed only after an incident.
gaap: ASC 450-20 — loss contingencies from uninsured contractor work
COSO 2013 — Principle 9, risks arising from third-party relationships
SOC 1 — data leaving the system boundary to a third-party platform
redFlags: Marketplace compliance status accepted in place of a property-specific certificate of insurance
Invitations sent to an email address supplied by the vendor without verification
Marketplace vendors engaged before internal vendor approval is complete
scr_ap_inviting_vendors_to_the_realpage_.yardi: Yardi Marketplace vendor onboarding with VendorCafe compliance document tracking.

scr_ap_guidelines_for_updating_vendors.purpose: The rules for bulk-updating vendor records by CSV import — data in the spreadsheet overwrites what is in the existing record, and a blank cell removes the corresponding information, so blanks must never be left unless removal is intended.
scr_ap_guidelines_for_updating_vendors.outcome: A bulk vendor update changes only the attributes intended, leaving every other field on each record untouched.
scr_ap_guidelines_for_updating_vendors.rootCause: The blank-means-delete rule turns a partial spreadsheet into a mass deletion. An analyst exporting vendor ID and phone to fix phone numbers, then importing that two-column file, wipes remit-to addresses, tax IDs and 1099 flags across the entire vendor master — and because an import applies as a single bulk operation, the change log records it as one event with no per-field review and no approval workflow in front of it. Bank and remit details can be rewritten at scale through a path the vendor-approval control never sees.
scr_ap_guidelines_for_updating_vendors.ifSkipped: A routine bulk update silently strips tax IDs, remit-to addresses and 1099 flags from hundreds of vendors, discovered at the next check run or at year-end.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 11, controls over bulk data changes
IRC §6109 — TIN retained on the vendor record
SOX 404 — change control over the vendor master
reports: Vendor master list before and after comparison
redFlags: Partial-column imports run against the live vendor master
Bulk vendor imports bypassing the vendor record approval workflow
No pre-import backup or post-import field-level comparison
scr_ap_guidelines_for_updating_vendors.yardi: Yardi Voyager: vendor import via ETL or the data import wizard, with the same overwrite semantics on supplied columns.

scr_ap_troubleshooting_vendor_restrictio.purpose: Diagnoses the errors that appear when a location is excluded from a vendor's restrictions while the vendor still holds an active account there — 'Location is invalid, enter valid location' on pending transactions, and 'Vendor has active storefront accounts for locations outside of locations restricted' on save — with the fix being to remove the vendor account from the location first, then exclude it.
scr_ap_troubleshooting_vendor_restrictio.outcome: The restriction takes effect cleanly and the property's open invoices for that vendor continue to process and pay.
scr_ap_troubleshooting_vendor_restrictio.rootCause: The ordering is what people get wrong, and the consequence lands on transactions already in flight. Restricting first strands every pending invoice for that property in an error state — they cannot be approved, cannot be paid, and will not appear in the payment run, so a vendor with legitimate open invoices simply stops being paid while nobody sees an alert. The invoices are not lost, but nothing surfaces them until the vendor calls.
scr_ap_troubleshooting_vendor_restrictio.ifSkipped: Pending invoices for the excluded location error out silently, age past terms, and the vendor's balance sits unpaid with no exception report pointing at it.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 12, configuration changes sequenced to avoid disrupting transactions
ASC 405-10 — the obligation persists even while the transaction errors
Vendor contract payment-terms obligations
redFlags: Restrictions applied before storefront accounts are removed from the location
Errored transactions with no monitoring report to surface them
Vendors reporting non-payment before the A/P team knows the invoices are stuck
scr_ap_troubleshooting_vendor_restrictio.yardi: Yardi Voyager: property-scope changes on a vendor blocking existing payables until the scope is corrected.

scr_ap_generate_account_number_page.purpose: Requests storefront vendor account numbers for properties from the vendor's Storefront supplier code link — selecting the properties, clicking Generate/Remove account number, checking the request status and closing the box, with a specific permission required unless the user holds administrator privileges.
scr_ap_generate_account_number_page.outcome: Each selected property receives its own account number with the storefront vendor, so ordering and billing can be attributed to the correct property.
scr_ap_generate_account_number_page.rootCause: Property-level account numbers are what make a national supply vendor's billing allocable. Without one, a supplier bills the management company in aggregate and the invoice arrives as a single line covering eight properties — which the accountant then splits by hand from a packing-slip reading exercise, producing an allocation that is an estimate presented as an actual on eight separate owner statements.
scr_ap_generate_account_number_page.ifSkipped: Storefront orders bill against a shared account, invoices arrive unallocated, and property-level expense coding becomes a manual estimate.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 13, information attributable to the correct reporting unit
ASC 720 — expense recognized by the entity that incurred it
Management agreement property-level accounting requirements
reports: Vendor master list with storefront codes
redFlags: Properties sharing one storefront account number across a portfolio
Account number requests left in pending status with nobody checking
Administrator privileges used to bypass the account-request permission control
