scr_ap_generate_account_number_page.yardi: Yardi Marketplace property-level supplier accounts driving per-property invoice allocation.

scr_ap_removing_a_vendor_account_from_a_.purpose: Detaches a property's online shopping account from a storefront vendor — open the vendor's Storefront supplier code link, click Remove next to the property in the Property table, then Generate/Remove account number to process it.
scr_ap_removing_a_vendor_account_from_a_.outcome: The property can no longer order through that vendor's storefront, while its posted purchase and payment history stays intact.
scr_ap_removing_a_vendor_account_from_a_.rootCause: Removal is the step that has to happen before a vendor restriction can be applied to the same location, and doing it in the wrong order produces the error condition that strands pending invoices. It also needs to happen when a property leaves the portfolio: an account left live at a disposed asset lets a site team that no longer reports to this manager keep ordering against a vendor relationship the former owner is still billed under.
scr_ap_removing_a_vendor_account_from_a_.ifSkipped: Storefront ordering stays open at properties that should no longer use the vendor, and subsequent restriction changes fail with account-conflict errors.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 10, timely removal of transaction access on disposition
IRC §6001 — posted purchase history retained after the account is removed
Property management agreement termination provisions
reports: Vendor master list with storefront codes
redFlags: Storefront accounts live at properties sold or transferred out of management
Removal attempted while open orders are still pending at the property
No storefront account review in the property offboarding checklist
scr_ap_removing_a_vendor_account_from_a_.yardi: Yardi Marketplace supplier account deactivation per property during offboarding.

scr_ap_changing_a_vendors_subscription_t.purpose: Switches a storefront vendor between Invoice Submission Service and Managed Catalog via More actions > Update subscription type on the Generate account number box, with the system emailing the vendor about the change and the confirmation message differing by direction.
scr_ap_changing_a_vendors_subscription_t.outcome: The vendor's billing route changes to match how the portfolio actually transacts with them, and the vendor is notified of the new arrangement.
scr_ap_changing_a_vendors_subscription_t.rootCause: The two subscription types produce structurally different invoices. Managed Catalog invoices carry priced catalog line items that match to a purchase order automatically; Invoice Submission Service invoices arrive as vendor-formatted documents requiring manual coding. Switching without telling the A/P team means invoices that previously auto-matched suddenly need hand-coding, and the ones sitting in flight at the moment of the switch match against nothing and fall into exception.
scr_ap_changing_a_vendors_subscription_t.ifSkipped: The vendor stays on a subscription type that does not fit how the portfolio buys from them, and invoice matching either fails or requires manual work on every document.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 12, change communicated to the people who operate the control
ASC 405-10 — liability recognized regardless of the invoice delivery route
Vendor agreement terms on billing method
reports: Vendor master list with subscription type
redFlags: Subscription switched with invoices already in flight under the old format
A/P team not informed, so matching exceptions spike with no explanation
Vendor notified by system email only, with no confirmation they acknowledged it
scr_ap_changing_a_vendors_subscription_t.yardi: Yardi Marketplace supplier configured as catalog versus non-catalog, changing how invoices match to purchase orders.

scr_ap_enabling_vendor_remittance_emails.purpose: Turns on the Send automatic payment notification check box in the Payment details section of a vendor's Payment information tab, which also covers the case of an invoice paid in full by applying a credit rather than cash.
scr_ap_enabling_vendor_remittance_emails.outcome: That vendor automatically receives remittance detail on every payment, including credit-only settlements where no funds move.
scr_ap_enabling_vendor_remittance_emails.rootCause: The credit-applied case is the reason to be deliberate about this flag. A remittance advice arriving for an invoice settled entirely from a credit memo looks like payment notification, and vendors routinely post it as cash received — creating a difference between the vendor's ledger and the property's that only surfaces when the vendor statement is reconciled months later. Enabling it per vendor also scatters the setting, so half the vendor master gets remittances and the other half does not, with no report showing which.
scr_ap_enabling_vendor_remittance_emails.ifSkipped: Vendors receive no payment detail, apply cash against the wrong invoices, and vendor statements stop agreeing to the property's A/P aging.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 14, communicating with external parties
ASC 405-20 — liability extinguished by credit application rather than cash
SOC 1 — outbound transmission of payment detail
redFlags: Credit-only remittances misread by vendors as cash payments
Remittance enabled inconsistently across the vendor master with no coverage report
Remittance emails routed to an address never confirmed with the vendor
scr_ap_enabling_vendor_remittance_emails.yardi: Yardi Voyager: automatic remittance email on check and EFT payments, set per vendor in the payment configuration.

scr_ap_vendor_totals_page.purpose: Shows how much each entity owes a given vendor, with the guidance to run the Vendor Aging report filtered on the vendor and property, using the Detail report type with Include G/L detail, when more than the total is needed.
scr_ap_vendor_totals_page.outcome: A vendor's exposure is broken out by entity, so an intercompany or multi-owner balance is visible rather than hidden inside a single number.
scr_ap_vendor_totals_page.rootCause: One vendor serving eight properties across three ownership entities produces a total that belongs to nobody. The entity split is what makes it useful — and what reveals when one entity has been carrying another's payables, a Due To/Due From condition that must be settled rather than netted. The page gives totals only; the G/L detail behind them requires the aging report, and skipping that step means the reviewer sees a balance without knowing which accounts it sits in.
scr_ap_vendor_totals_page.ifSkipped: Vendor exposure is quoted as one portfolio-wide figure, intercompany carrying is invisible, and the balance cannot be tied to any entity's 2010 Accounts Payable.
gaap: ASC 850 — related-party balances between entities under common control
ASC 405-10 — liability presented by the obligated entity
ASC 810 — consolidation and elimination of intercompany balances
redFlags: One entity consistently carrying payables for another with no settlement
Vendor totals quoted without the supporting aging detail
Entity balances that do not sum to the vendor's control account total
scr_ap_vendor_totals_page.yardi: Yardi Voyager: vendor ledger filtered by property with the Payable Aging report at detail level including GL accounts.

scr_ap_viewing_vendor_totals.purpose: The act of opening those totals from the Vendors list — clicking the Total due column, which shows either a currency figure or a View due link depending on whether the company is multi-entity and multi-base-currency.
scr_ap_viewing_vendor_totals.outcome: The person asking what a vendor is owed gets the answer from the list in one click, in the correct form for the company's entity structure.
scr_ap_viewing_vendor_totals.rootCause: Whether the column shows a number or a link is itself information, and it is routinely misread. A currency figure means one entity and one base currency; a View due link means the balance cannot be expressed as a single amount at all. Quoting the figure from a screenshot, or exporting the column and totaling it, produces a vendor exposure number that mixes currencies — and that number ends up in an owner email or a contract dispute before anyone checks how it was derived.
scr_ap_viewing_vendor_totals.ifSkipped: Vendor balance questions require running a report each time, and the quick answer given verbally is an unverified number.
gaap: ASC 830 — foreign currency balances not aggregated at face value
ASC 405-10 — accurate presentation of amounts owed
COSO 2013 — Principle 13, quality of information used externally
redFlags: Total due column summed across entities in different base currencies
Balances quoted to vendors or owners from the list without tying to the aging
A View due link ignored and the underlying entity split never opened
scr_ap_viewing_vendor_totals.yardi: Yardi Voyager: open balance shown on the vendor search list, drilling into the vendor ledger for the detail.

scr_ap_changing_a_vendors_address.purpose: Edits the address fields in the Primary contact section of a vendor record from Accounts Payable > Search & Find > Vendors > Edit, the ordinary path for a vendor that has relocated or changed its remit-to.
scr_ap_changing_a_vendors_address.outcome: Future payments and correspondence go to the vendor's current address, and the change is captured in the vendor master change log.
scr_ap_changing_a_vendors_address.rootCause: Address changes are the most common vector for payment-diversion fraud in property management, and they almost always arrive as a plausible email on the vendor's letterhead. The control is a call-back to a phone number already on file — never the number in the request — performed by someone other than the person making the edit. An address change is also a 1099 event: a form mailed to a stale address comes back undeliverable, and IRC §6722 penalties attach to the payee statement regardless of whose address was wrong.
scr_ap_changing_a_vendors_address.ifSkipped: Checks and 1099 forms go to an old address, come back undeliverable, and a fraudulent change request is executed with no independent verification.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 10, independent verification of payment destination changes
IRC §6722 — penalties for incorrect payee statements
AU-C 240 — fraud risk from vendor master manipulation
redFlags: Address changes made from an emailed request with no call-back to a known number
Address changed and an invoice for the same vendor paid within the same day
The person who changed the address also holding payment release rights
scr_ap_changing_a_vendors_address.yardi: Yardi Voyager: vendor remit-to address edit, with the change captured in the vendor audit trail.

scr_ap_viewing_the_a_p_invoices_list.purpose: Reaching the A/P invoices list from Accounts Payable > Search & find > A/P invoices, the entry point for locating any invoice in the system regardless of its status.
scr_ap_viewing_the_a_p_invoices_list.outcome: The accountant lands on the working population of invoices and can filter from there to the specific document, vendor or period in question.
scr_ap_viewing_the_a_p_invoices_list.rootCause: What loads on arrival is not the full invoice population, and the default is where audit requests go wrong. An auditor asking for an invoice they can see on the prior-year aging will be told it does not exist, because the list opened with the current period or the last-90-days filter still set from the previous session. The accountant's honest answer is wrong, and the PBC item comes back as an exception.
scr_ap_viewing_the_a_p_invoices_list.ifSkipped: Invoice lookups start from reports rather than the live list, and the accountant works from a static extract that is stale the moment a batch posts.
gaap: COSO 2013 — Principle 13, complete information for the question being asked
IRC §6001 — retrievable transaction records
SOX 404 — evidence produced from the complete population
redFlags: Prior-period invoices reported as missing because the default filter excluded them
Persistent filter state carried between sessions without being checked
Searches run at entity level when the invoice was entered at top level
scr_ap_viewing_the_a_p_invoices_list.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Payable Search across all periods, or the Payable Register filtered by property and date range.

scr_ap_a_p_invoices_list.purpose: The A/P invoices list itself — add, view, edit, print, delete or reverse an unpaid invoice, import and export — carrying the Hold column, the State column that links to approval history and shows Submitted or Declined, the Include private and Show future draft invoices switches, the 90-day filter, per-column filter boxes, invoice packaging via the Select check boxes, and custom views for columns such as Payment method and Payment number.
scr_ap_a_p_invoices_list.outcome: A single working surface for the whole invoice population, from which an accountant can see status, hold condition and approval state without opening each record.
scr_ap_a_p_invoices_list.rootCause: Three defaults on this list each hide a different category, and together they can produce a check run that looks complete and is not. Show A/P invoices in the last 90 days drops the aged item an owner is asking about; Include private, on by default, can be cleared and quietly remove every entity-level invoice; and future draft invoices stay hidden unless explicitly requested. Each one is a legitimate convenience and each one changes what an approver believes they are looking at.
scr_ap_a_p_invoices_list.ifSkipped: Invoice status, holds and approval state are chased through separate reports, and the team loses the one view that shows a held invoice next to its approval history.
gaap: ASC 405-10 — completeness of recorded liabilities
COSO 2013 — Principle 13, the control operates over the full population
SOX 404 — review evidence covering all items in scope
redFlags: Check-run review performed with the 90-day filter active
Include private cleared, hiding entity-level invoices from a top-level reviewer
Held and declined invoices with no owner and no follow-up date
scr_ap_a_p_invoices_list.yardi: Yardi Voyager: Payables > Payable Register with hold status, workflow state and per-column filtering.

scr_ap_showing_a_p_invoices_in_the_last_.purpose: The Show A/P Invoices in the last 90 days check box, which narrows the list to invoices whose invoice date falls in that window and excludes everything older.
scr_ap_showing_a_p_invoices_in_the_last_.outcome: A fast working list for current-cycle processing, holding roughly a quarter of invoice activity instead of the full history.
scr_ap_showing_a_p_invoices_in_the_last_.rootCause: The filter keys on invoice date, not entry date or posting date, and that distinction is where it does damage. A vendor who bills six months late submits an invoice dated outside the window on the day it arrives, so it is excluded from the list the moment it is entered — invisible in the working view while sitting in 2010 Accounts Payable. At close, an accountant reviewing unpaid invoices from this list misses precisely the aged items that need an accrual decision or a stale-payable write-back review.
scr_ap_showing_a_p_invoices_in_the_last_.ifSkipped: The list loads the entire invoice history, which is slow on a large portfolio and buries current work in years of settled activity.
gaap: ASC 405-10 — aged liabilities remain recognized until settled or released
COSO 2013 — Principle 13, filtered views not mistaken for the population
State unclaimed property statutes — aged unpaid items eventually escheat
redFlags: Late-dated vendor invoices excluded from the working list the day they are entered
Month-end unpaid invoice review run with the filter on
Aged payables never reviewed because they never appear in the default view
scr_ap_showing_a_p_invoices_in_the_last_.yardi: Yardi Voyager: payable search date-range filters, which likewise key on invoice date rather than entry date.

scr_ap_adding_the_location_to_the_a_p_in.purpose: Builds a custom view that adds the Location name column to the A/P invoices list — selecting it in step one, positioning it in the column sequence, then saving the view under a name such as Locations included — so the list shows where the money was spent.
scr_ap_adding_the_location_to_the_a_p_in.outcome: Invoices display the property they belong to, making a multi-property list readable and misallocations visible at a glance.
scr_ap_adding_the_location_to_the_a_p_in.rootCause: Without the location column a portfolio-level invoice list is a wall of vendors and amounts with no way to see which property bears each cost. That is how a shared-vendor invoice gets reviewed and approved with the wrong property attached: the coding is correct on the invoice record but the reviewer never sees it in the list, and the misallocation surfaces in the owner's operating statement as an expense at a property that never received the service. Reversing it after the owner package ships means a prior-period correction and a conversation with the asset manager.
scr_ap_adding_the_location_to_the_a_p_in.ifSkipped: Multi-property invoice lists show no property attribution, and misallocated costs are caught only when an owner queries their variance.
gaap: ASC 720 — expense recognized by the entity that incurred it
ASC 850 — costs borne by one entity for another
Management agreement property-level accounting requirements
redFlags: Invoice review performed on a list with no location column
Shared-vendor invoices consistently landing on one property
Custom view saved privately, so only its creator ever sees location
scr_ap_adding_the_location_to_the_a_p_in.yardi: Yardi Voyager: adding the property column to a payable register filter set, saved as a named report layout.

scr_ap_adding_the_g_l_account_number_col.purpose: Creates a custom view through Manage views > Create new view that includes the G/L account number column, saved under a meaningful name and loaded from the All drop-down, then filtered by typing the first digits of an account into the column filter box.
scr_ap_adding_the_g_l_account_number_col.outcome: Invoices can be listed and filtered by the expense account they were coded to, turning the invoice list into a coding-review tool.
scr_ap_adding_the_g_l_account_number_col.rootCause: This is the fastest capital-versus-repair review available in the system: filter to 6110 Repairs & Maintenance and read the vendor and description on every line. Roof work, HVAC replacement and flooring sitting in 6110 rather than 1530 Building Improvements is a Treas. Reg. §1.263(a)-3 problem that overstates the expense, understates NOI and understates the depreciable basis — and it is invisible on any list that does not carry the account number. The same view filtered to 1310 Prepaid Expenses catches insurance and service contracts that were expensed in full instead of amortized.
scr_ap_adding_the_g_l_account_number_col.ifSkipped: Coding review happens invoice by invoice or not at all, and capital items expensed in error surface at the fixed-asset rollforward or in the tax return.
gaap: Treas. Reg. §1.263(a)-3 — betterment, restoration and adaptation tests
ASC 360-10 — capitalization of costs extending useful life
IRC §6662 — accuracy-related penalty where deductions are misstated
reports: A/P invoice register by GL account
redFlags: Large single-vendor amounts sitting in 6110 Repairs & Maintenance
Annual insurance and service contracts expensed rather than routed through 1310 Prepaid Expenses
GL-coded review view created once and never used during the close
scr_ap_adding_the_g_l_account_number_col.yardi: Yardi Voyager: payable register with the GL account column and account filter, used for the capital-versus-repair scrub.

scr_ap_adding_the_attachment_column_to_a.purpose: Adds the Attachment column to a custom view of the A/P invoices list, showing Yes or No per invoice, with the filter typed as 'Yes' in the column filter box and then baked into the saved view through Manage views > Edit > Select filters.
scr_ap_adding_the_attachment_column_to_a.outcome: Invoices with and without supporting documents are distinguishable in the list, and a saved view can isolate either set on demand.
scr_ap_adding_the_attachment_column_to_a.rootCause: Filtering this view to Yes is the mistake that matters. Saved as a default, it produces a list containing only documented invoices — so the invoices with no backing document, the exact population a reviewer needs to chase, become invisible in the very view built to manage attachments. The useful filter is No: those are the invoices the auditor will select and the ones the IRS can disallow under IRC §6001 for want of a source document.
scr_ap_adding_the_attachment_column_to_a.ifSkipped: Nobody can tell which invoices lack supporting documents until an auditor samples one and the backup cannot be produced.
gaap: IRC §6001 and Treas. Reg. §1.6001-1 — source documents supporting every deduction
Rev. Proc. 98-25 — electronic records complete, legible and retrievable

scr_ap_exporting_the_a_p_invoices_list.purpose: Exports any view of the A/P invoices list, up to 25,000 rows at a time, to the browser's default download location for analysis, owner packages or audit evidence outside the system.
scr_ap_exporting_the_a_p_invoices_list.outcome: The filtered invoice population leaves the system as a file that can be pivoted, tied out to the control account and attached to a work paper.
scr_ap_exporting_the_a_p_invoices_list.rootCause: The 25,000-row cap truncates silently on a large portfolio's full-year export, and the file gives no indication it is incomplete — so a tie-out to 2010 Accounts Payable fails by an amount the accountant then spends a day hunting for. The export also carries the applied view's filters with it, meaning a file exported from a 90-day or attachment-filtered view is a subset presented as a population. Once it is an .xlsx on someone's laptop it is outside the SOC 1 boundary, still carrying vendor names, tax identifiers and payment detail.
scr_ap_exporting_the_a_p_invoices_list.ifSkipped: Analysis and owner requests are answered from screen reads, and there is no tie-out file to support the A/P balance in the month-end work papers.
